prompt: What does a fine-tuning run change?

choices.text: Its weights
choices.why: Right: after the run there is a new model with its own name.

choices.text: The tokenizer the provider counts with
choices.why: Training leaves the tokenizer as it was.

choices.text: The documents in the vector index
choices.why: Fine-tuning never touches the index.

choices.text: The system prompt sent with each request
choices.why: That is a prompt change, free to make and undo.

prompt: Why is a fact learnt by fine-tuning held weakly, while a format is learnt well?

choices.text: Facts are stored in a different layer of the network
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson places facts in a layer; the argument is about repetition.

choices.text: Formats are shorter than facts
choices.why: Length is not the point; how often each is shown is.

choices.text: A format is in every example; a fact in one or two
choices.why: Right. Hundreds of examples push one way for the format, a couple for each fact.

choices.text: Providers block facts from training data
choices.why: Facts can be in the data; they are just learnt weakly.

prompt: What was wrong with the second line of ft.jsonl?
hint: Which policy did the retrieval step find?

choices.text: It taught the 2025 postage rule
choices.why: Right: the replaced policy went into the training data, unmarked.

choices.text: It had no assistant message
choices.why: It has one: the wrong answer.

choices.text: Its JSON was not valid
choices.why: The line is valid JSON; its content is the problem.

choices.text: It used the question of another example
choices.why: The question matches the test set; the answer is stale.

prompt: How many training tokens per epoch did dataset.py count?
How many tokens did reindex_cost.py count for every section of every document?
The lesson says the bottleneck in keeping a RAG system fresh is not the embedding. What is it?
hint: Under a second is not the problem.

choices.text: Waiting for the vector database to rebuild its whole index
choices.why: Only changed chunks need to change.

choices.text: Retraining the generator on the new policy
choices.why: A RAG system does not retrain anything.

choices.text: Noticing that a document changed
choices.why: Right; lesson 5 stores a hash of each chunk to find exactly what changed.

choices.text: Paying the embedding provider for every section of every document
choices.why: A few cents at most; not the bottleneck.

prompt: A carrier goes on strike and the help centre gets a delays banner at 10 am. Which assistant mentions the delays to a customer at 10:05?
hint: Which one reads the help centre at question time?

choices.text: Neither; strikes are outside any document
choices.why: The banner is a document, and the runbook says to publish it.

choices.text: The one that retrieves at question time
choices.why: Right: the banner is in the index from the moment it is embedded.

choices.text: Both, since the banner is short
choices.why: Length does not put it in a model's weights.

choices.text: One fine-tuned last week on the help centre
choices.why: Last week the banner did not exist.

prompt: In the traceability run, which document did [1] point at?

choices.text: terms-of-sale
choices.why: It was not in the top three.

choices.text: returns-policy-2025
choices.why: Right, at 0.807, which is why the reply led with fourteen days.

choices.text: ft.jsonl
choices.why: That is the training set, not a document in the index.

choices.text: returns-policy
choices.why: That was [2], at 0.798.

prompt: A fine-tuned model is trained to end every reply with a citation like [returns-policy]. Why is that weaker than a RAG citation?
hint: Was the cited text in front of the model?

choices.text: It is learnt text, not a pointer to what the model read
choices.why: Right. Only retrieval puts the cited text in the prompt at answer time.

choices.text: Fine-tuned models cannot output square brackets
choices.why: They can write any text their examples showed.

choices.text: The citation format differs from the one RAG systems use
choices.why: Format is not the problem; what stands behind it is.

choices.text: Providers remove citations from fine-tuned replies
choices.why: Nothing removes them; they just mean less.

prompt: What does a citation that points at retrieved text make possible? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three things, in the lesson's list.

choices.text: A person checking the answer without trusting the model
choices.why: Yes, by opening the source.

choices.text: Guaranteeing that the cited document is current
choices.why: No: [1] pointed at the 2025 policy. The citation shows it; it does not prevent it.

choices.text: Removing the need for a test set
choices.why: No: lesson 8 measures quality with one.

choices.text: Proving what the organisation told a customer and why
choices.why: Yes, in a dispute or to a regulator.

choices.text: Telling retrieval failures from generation failures
choices.why: Yes: the citation says what the generator was shown.

prompt: A RAG answer can be traced because each claim carries a ___ to the text the model was shown.
On average, how many retrieved tokens did a test-set question add to the prompt?
Why does the lesson call the first costs.py run, with fine-tuning at 0.29 a month, misleading?

choices.text: It left out the 30,000 questions
choices.why: Questions only enter the retrieval line.

choices.text: It counted epochs twice
choices.why: Three epochs, counted once.

choices.text: Twenty-six examples do not teach a model a corpus
choices.why: Right; facts need many phrasings, so the real dataset is far larger.

choices.text: The prices typed were too low
choices.why: The same prices were used in both runs.

prompt: At the lesson's illustrative 3 per million input tokens, how many questions a month make 332 tokens of context cost 290.40? Round to the nearest thousand.
Marginalia's policies start changing eight times a month instead of four. What happens to the two lines in the figure?
hint: Which line depends on the number of retrains?

choices.text: Both double
choices.why: The retrieval line depends on questions, not changes.

choices.text: Fine-tuning doubles; retrieval stays
choices.why: Right, and the crossing point moves to twice as many questions.

choices.text: Neither moves
choices.why: Each change is a retraining run on the fine-tuning side.

choices.text: Retrieval doubles; fine-tuning stays
choices.why: Re-indexing changed documents is almost free; the context per question is unchanged.

prompt: How does a retrieval system stop knowing a withdrawn document?

choices.text: By retraining the embedding model
choices.why: The embedding model has nothing to unlearn; the chunks are the knowledge.

choices.text: By adding an instruction to ignore it
choices.why: The text would still be retrieved and put in the prompt.

choices.text: By deleting the document's chunks from the index
choices.why: Right; the next question cannot find what is not there.

choices.text: By lowering its similarity scores
choices.why: Scores are computed, not set; and a low score can still be retrieved.

prompt: What changed in the label-cost reply when the 2025 policy was left out?

choices.text: It stopped contradicting itself
choices.why: Right: only the current rule was left.

choices.text: It cited the warehouse runbook
choices.why: The runbook was retrieved but not quoted.

choices.text: It refused, since nothing scored high enough
choices.why: It answered from the current policy.

choices.text: It said the label costs 4.50 instead of free
choices.why: That was the 2025 sentence, which disappeared.

prompt: A customer asks Marginalia to delete their data, and their support chats were used to fine-tune the assistant. What can the team guarantee?

choices.text: Removing the chats from the dataset removes them from the model
choices.why: The model was already trained; the dataset no longer matters to it.

choices.text: Little, short of retraining without the chats
choices.why: Right. That is why personal data belongs in an index, where it can be deleted.

choices.text: An output filter guarantees the name never appears
choices.why: It catches the exact wording and nothing else.

choices.text: Training on top with opposite examples erases it
choices.why: It makes repeating less likely; it guarantees nothing.

prompt: Which of these is a job fine-tuning does well?

choices.text: Returning the same JSON shape every time
choices.why: Right: a pattern repeated in every example.

choices.text: Showing finance documents only to finance
choices.why: One model knows the same for everybody.

choices.text: Letting a support lead see why an answer was given
choices.why: That is traceability, which fine-tuning cannot give.

choices.text: Keeping the assistant's prices up to date
choices.why: Prices are facts that change; retrieval's job.

prompt: Training a small, cheap model on the replies of a large, expensive one, so it does one narrow job nearly as well, is called ___.
A team's system prompt has grown to a page of style rules and twenty examples, and it runs two million times a month. What does the lesson suggest?
hint: The page is paid for on every request.

choices.text: Add more examples to the prompt until it holds
choices.why: That makes every one of two million requests dearer.

choices.text: Fine-tune the style; keep retrieving facts
choices.why: Right: the page moves into the weights, the facts stay retrievable.

choices.text: Move the policies into the weights too, to save more
choices.why: Facts stay in documents; only the behaviour moves.

choices.text: Delete the style rules and accept the drift
choices.why: The prompt proved the behaviour is worth having.

prompt: Put in order the approaches the lesson says to try, from first to last.
items: Instructions and examples in the prompt
Fine-tuning for behaviour prompts cannot hold

prompt: Match each need to the approach the lesson's table gives it.

pairs.left: A strict format in every reply

pairs.right: a filter on what is retrieved

prompt: In the lesson's combined design, what does fine-tuning decide and what does retrieval decide?

choices.text: Fine-tuning the facts; retrieval the format
choices.why: The facts are what must never cross into the weights.

choices.text: Both decide everything, by voting
choices.why: They have separate jobs.

choices.text: Fine-tuning which sources; retrieval how to cite them
choices.why: Reversed: training cannot choose this question's sources.

choices.text: Fine-tuning how to use a source; retrieval which sources
choices.why: Right.

prompt: Which question is about behaviour rather than knowledge?
hint: Would the answer change if a policy changed?

choices.text: Which carriers deliver express orders?
choices.why: A fact about operations; knowledge.

choices.text: What is the affiliate commission on e-books?
choices.why: A number in a document; knowledge.

choices.text: Should the answer come first?
choices.why: Right: a pattern in every reply, whatever the policy says.

choices.text: How long is a gift card valid?
choices.why: A fact that could change; knowledge.
